author: EmuCore - Hub
title: An exhaustive look at extracting graphics from PS1 and PS2 games
summary: Hilltop dedicates ninety-five minutes to extracting graphics from PlayStation and PlayStation 2 games, preserving a research-oriented workflow relevant to translation patches, documentation and asset archaeology rather than a quick texture-pack install.

blocks.text: The exceptional length signals that “extracting graphics” is not one operation shared by every game. A researcher may need to locate containers, distinguish palettes from pixel data, infer dimensions, test decompression and verify how pieces are assembled at runtime. Hilltop’s channel context—English patches and credited projects—places the work near practical preservation rather than a showcase of ripped images. For Hub readers, the session demonstrates why file-format knowledge and repeatable export tools matter when visual text or interface assets must be studied.

Public notes omit chapters, named games, tool versions, repository and a written format specification, so individual techniques must be confirmed from the footage and should not be generalized across PS1 and PS2 engines. Extracted art remains copyrighted even when research tooling is original. Work from lawfully obtained personal data, publish code and documentation rather than proprietary asset archives, and record hashes before editing. Treat the stream as a deep exploratory source; stable automation requires independent validation against multiple files and game revisions.
